topic: Ironic Process Theory (The White Bear Problem)
title: Why Trying Not to Think About Something Guarantees You Will
coreConcept: The brain cannot search for what to avoid without first activating the mental representation of what is forbidden.
sources: Wegner et al. (1987), J Pers Soc Psychol

topic: The Trolley Problem: Footbridge Dilemma (Greene Neuroimaging)
title: Why We Convince Ourselves Boring Tasks Were Fun
coreConcept: When external rewards cannot justify our actions, the brain manufactures internal conviction.
sources: Festinger & Carlsmith (1959), J Abnorm Soc Psychol

title: Why You Forget Why You Entered a Room
coreConcept: Walking through doorways creates mental event boundaries in episodic memory.
sources: Radvansky et al. (2011), Q J Exp Psychol

title: Doing Someone a Favor Makes You Like Them More
coreConcept: Cognitive dissonance drives us to justify our kind actions by concluding we must like the recipient.

title: Why the Best Comebacks Only Arrive When It’s Too Late
coreConcept: Acute social stress floods prefrontal working memory; subsequent relaxation permits divergent associative recall.
